finding.claim: dropTable never enforces its 'dba' role check: Authorize's error return is discarded, so any caller that reaches /admin/drop with a user in context executes the DROP regardless of role.
finding.source: Any authenticated request to /admin/drop (user context set by middleware outside this file); user roles are irrelevant because the result is ignored.

trace.note: /admin/drop routed to dropTable with no authorization wrapper
u := userFrom(r) obtains the user from request context
Authorize(u, "dba") called as a bare statement; error return dropped

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) correctly returns 'forbidden' for a missing role, but its result is never read at api.go:26. No route-level middleware is visible in api.go:44. Contrast with vacuum (api.go:33-36), which correctly gates on the error. userFrom (api.go:22) panics on a missing user before the sink, so it is not a bypass. Middleware outside this directory was not visible and could add a gate; this must be confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. Authorize (api.go:13-20) does return "forbidden" for a missing role, but its result is discarded as a bare call at api.go:26, so runSQL at api.go:27 runs unconditionally. /admin/drop is registered with no wrapper at api.go:44. The only other guard is userFrom (api.go:22), which panics on a missing user and is not a bypass. The vacuum handler (api.go:33-36) checks the error correctly, which confirms the drop handler is the defect.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: Authorize's error is discarded at api.go:26 and runSQL executes the DROP at api.go:27 for any request that has a user in context. The attacker is any authenticated user, not only a DBA, but the file set contains no auth middleware, so reachability by a low-privilege user depends on middleware outside this directory that sets the user context. The code-level flaw is confirmed either way.

finding.claim: Table name from a form parameter is concatenated into a DDL statement with no allowlist or quoting, enabling SQL injection into runSQL.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (query string or form body, attacker-controlled)

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") read and concatenated into the DROP TABLE string
string passed to runSQL; the body of runSQL is a stub (api.go:41), so the SQL sink is inferred from its name and signature

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, quoting, or parameter binding on 't'. The only gate is the authorization check, which is ineffective (AUTHZ-1). Identifiers cannot be bound as parameters, so the fix is an allowlist of table names. Stacked-statement injection depends on the driver, which is not visible. Impact is any table drop or arbitrary statement, reachable by any caller with a user in context. The decoy 25-decoy-identifier-allowlist does not apply because no allowlist exists here.

verdict.guard_found: The only candidate control is the Authorize("dba") call at api.go:26, which is a bare statement whose error return is discarded, so it blocks nothing. No allowlist, quoting, or parameter binding on "t" exists at api.go:27. Only api.go is present in the directory, so no middleware or real runSQL body is visible.
verdict.reason: The route at api.go:44 reaches dropTable, where r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 is concatenated into "DROP TABLE " and passed to runSQL, while the Authorize result at api.go:26 is ignored, so any caller with a user in context (api.go:25) reaches it. The SQL effect is inferred because runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, and stacked-statement or arbitrary-statement impact depends on the driver, which is not visible.
